minutes.headline: Board weighed shared-drainage liability on two subdivisions and approved a bond so 181 Electric Ave can get its occupancy permit
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Planning Board continued public hearings on storm water permits for new house lots at 222 West Townsend Road and Zero Reservoir Road, with abutters raising well-water and runoff concerns at the former and the board pressing at length over who is responsible for maintaining a shared drainage system at the latter. In other business the board accepted a bond to let 181 Electric Avenue obtain an occupancy permit, adopted a revised fee schedule and revised storm water permit conditions, and voted to tell the select board it did not want to pursue the right of first refusal on 35 Lemonster Road.

what_happened.line: The board directed the applicant at Zero Reservoir Road to draft easement or deed language for a shared drainage system, for town counsel to review.
The board accepted a bond, in the amount as heard, so 181 Electric Avenue can get its occupancy permit, holding release until year-end.
The board voted to tell the select board it does not want to pursue the town's right of first refusal on 35 Lemonster Road.
Storm water permit hearings for new house lots at 222 West Townsend Road and Zero Reservoir Road were continued to 27 April after abutters raised well and runoff concerns.
The board adopted a revised, simplified fee schedule for storm water and plan-review permits after comparing fees to surrounding towns.

why_it_matters: Who maintains a subdivision's shared drainage system determines who pays if it fails later, a question that follows the property rather than the builder.
The bond lets an occupancy permit issue now while tying its release to stabilization work checked over two growing seasons, not verified immediately.
Declining the right of first refusal is a vote that forgoes the town's option to buy 35 Lemonster Road, relevant to residents tracking open space and land purchases.
